findings.explanation: The root describes the paper, analysis and inputs; its registered data and classifier modules lead to the paths actually read by the analysis. The private acquisition submodule is upstream of the published raw inputs, rather than a required input to the paper procedure. Anchor 3 is supported for this boundary.

The loader identifies the nested Andersson MAT files, studyforrest globs identify raw and event data, and even manually copied comparison statistics have an exact upstream MAT locator. No missing essential data/code reference was established; withheld payloads do not reduce this reachability score.

Environment recipe, saved image selection, analysis switches, default subjects and conversion factors are represented. This criterion asks whether ingredients are represented, so moving dependency versions and imperfect host setup instructions do not independently defeat anchor 3.

MIT, PDDL, GPLv3 and the root CC-BY text are reachable through registered modules. The complete supplied label-module inventory contains no license declaration, establishing a sufficient gap for anchor 2. Missing style/image payloads support uncertainty about their terms, not a definitive claim that their bytes contain no notices.

Root and nested Git object identities select code, data and results; annex keys and image digests identify payload states. The image display tag latest does not replace the recorded configuration/layer identities. Anchor 3 concerns identification, not downloaded-byte verification.

The frozen graph and tracked inventories connect ordinary Git objects, Gitlinks and annex references through a common root. External blob hosting does not place those content identities outside the integrated tracking system.

Inspected source histories contain actors, dated changes and descriptions for root manuscript/environment changes, raw-data imports, labels, classifier changes and evaluation inputs. This supports the modification-history anchor without treating self-reported authorship as authenticated identity.

The two DataLad records actually contain recorded commands, input declarations, output declarations and exit status. The signal-loss/velocity-histogram computation is absent from the dispatcher despite manuscript use, and no captured PDF build was identified. Partial provenance coverage is supported.

The main record identifies the image as an extra input and lives in a versioned dataset state. The label record invokes a shell script whose Python and inherited PYTHONPATH are not bound to an exact historical environment. That is a concrete reason to stop at anchor 2.

The cached annotated tag has a PGP signature and names a tagger, but neither it nor the inspected root supplies an identity-binding verification route. The binary zero is consistent with the full anchor; this is not a failed cryptographic verification claim.

Clone plus rerun is an explicit acquisition sequence; recorded input globs include raw data, event labels, evaluation data and the saved image. Git-tracked manuscript assets arrive with the root. Instructions can be credited independently of present-day retrieval verification.

The main run and PDF have commands, but the promised all-results sequence omits quality_stats, and flowchart_figs is marked not to be executed. The quality_stats docstring does provide a source-edit hint, so the claim should be lack of a complete command sequence rather than total absence of guidance; anchor 1 remains supported by other omitted figure steps.

The supplied executable acquisition path and the recorded input globs cover the paper input set and image. The dormant quality function uses the same explicitly declared raw-data family. Lack of permission to run retrieval does not itself defeat this procedure-based anchor.

Make targets and the Python dispatcher specify a substantial result-producing procedure. Including quality_stats requires a source change from prose and illustrative flowchart code does not save the final figures. Anchor 2 appropriately distinguishes these gaps from mere executable fragments.

The main record supplies a DataLad replay route with data and image inputs, whereas the label run leaves historical host state unresolved. That suffices for partial replay capability. The lack of a manuscript record is relevant to provenance coverage, but A-06 specifically asks about computations represented in provenance.

Registered data/classifier modules and separate code, container, figure and manuscript locations have identifiable responsibilities and explicit connections. Co-location of result definitions with manuscript sources does not by itself erase these module roles.

The paper imports remodnav.tests.utils and relies on nested tests/data storage, whereas the documented classifier interface is a CLI with named input/output arguments. Independent commits exist, but these consumer dependencies justify the limited-interface anchor.

Some declarations are explicitly attributable to individual modules, especially the classifier MIT statement and raw-data PDDL badge. The label module has no declaration in its tracked inventory. Anchor 2 follows without assuming the root license covers all linked components.

Several license identities are supplied, but the inspected root/module materials do not discuss their combination. This matches anchor 1; it does not establish a legal incompatibility or require the reviewer to infer one.

The rationale says access conditions cannot be determined for all components and therefore no anchor can be selected. M-05 explicitly includes that condition in anchor 0: access conditions cannot be determined. Null misapplies the native unknown-handling rule here. Missing license declarations should also be kept separate from access authorization requirements.
findings.suggested_correction: Use score 0 with a documented not_findable/observed limitation if access conditions remain undetermined, or supply evidence of uniform public access to justify 3. Do not assert that a restriction exists merely because a license is absent. Recompute completion after the change.

The root tree selects a joint state through Gitlinks, file objects and annex/image identities. Different selected classifier revisions in separate modules are explicit choices, not floating references. Coherent selection does not imply that the 2023 tag and 2025 root are identical or that all payloads are currently obtainable.

A signed results tag and recorded Docker build are distinct pieces of evidence. Neither supplies a verified producer/build-source attestation for the current executable image. The binary zero follows without claiming that content hashes authenticate the producer.

limitations: Inspection-only review of the assigned anonymized input, exact rubric, and frozen manifest cohort remodnav-e3c6253bced7. No peer assessments or reviews were consulted.

No network access, scientific execution, container build, payload acquisition or signature verification was performed. Unprovided scientific data, image layers and figure/style payloads are cohort limitations, not observed retrieval failures.

The root and its registered links established discovery paths. The DataLad Docker adapter was inspected only as the manifest-supplied external source reached from the root tool/version reference; its tag URL is not a commit pin, so this review identifies the frozen copy by SHA256.

The native validator accepted the bundle, but substantive judgments were independently checked. All 36 criterion IDs are present; 33 scores are non-null. Null A-02, M-05 and D-01 remain in their fixed dimension denominators and the native assessment is provisional. No stored numeric total or exclusion was present to contradict those rules.

The current Docker paper workflow consumes already-produced labels. Positive current-environment findings do not establish freshness, exact environment identity or successful replay of historical label generation.
Observed runtime model identity was not independently established. Agreement in this review is not human approval.
